title: Add audit-prooflet envelope and RBACv2 explainability endpoint
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We need stronger, verifiable audit metadata for tenant-scoped operations and more usable RBACv2 explanations for auditors. This PR introduces an 'audit-prooflet' envelope (compressed, signed metadata blobs) that KMS can attest to and a new internal-only API /internal/rbac/explain that returns deterministic decision traces for RBACv2 policy decisions. Motivation: existing audit headers are verbose and often out-of-band; auditors requested compact cryptographic proof attachments that can be validated independently and the security team requested a machine-readable explainability endpoint to debug policy regressions in canary rollouts.

What this PR does (summary): 1) Adds audit-prooflet envelope format and signing flow (api/audit/prooflet.go, infra/kms/prooflet_signer.go). 2) Plumbs prooflet creation into request ingest: prooflets are created at the audit-ingress stage and stored as compressed blobs in the audit-indexer with a KMS signature reference. 3) Adds /internal/rbac/explain endpoint (api/rbac/explain_handler.go) which returns a sanitized, canonical decision trace and the prooflet reference for the decision. 4) Adds DB migration to add prooflet index column (migrations/20241118_add_prooflet_index.sql) and a background backfill job (jobs/prooflet_backfill.go). 5) Console telemetry: exposes a read-only prooflet verification status and latency histogram. 6) Tests: unit tests for signing/verifying, integration test against kms-fake that simulates failure cases, and a small e2e that verifies a labeled tenant can request explains.

Design notes: - Prooflets are intentionally small (max 8KB) and use zlib compression + JSON-LD footprint to make them verifiable and language-agnostic. - KMS signer returns an ephemeral signature that includes a key-hash and region tag; we store the signature metadata with the prooflet index rather than embedding large KMS artifacts in the main audit row. - RBAC explain output is intentionally sanitized (no raw secrets, no long-lived tokens) and includes policy fingerprint, matched rules, evaluated claim set and short path to allow auditors to reproduce decisions offline. - Migration strategy: create the column as NULLABLE and enable prooflet creation behind a feature flag audit.prooflet.enabled defaulting to false; run backfill with tenant opt-in.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Deploy prooflet signer service in canary region and enable flag for internal tenants only. 3) Run backfill on a sample tenant cohort and verify prooflet integrity via a new admin tool proofletctl verify. 4) Gradually enable for all tenants over 4 weeks. 5) Add tenant-facing docs and sample verification script in redwood-examples.

Backward compatibility and safety: - If KMS signing fails we fall back to a plain audit header with a synthetic prooflet-ref stamped as "unsigned" and emit a telemetry metric audit.prooflet.sign_failure. - Prooflet size is enforced at creation time; oversized events are truncated with a deterministic hash to preserve reproducibility.

Testing and CI: - Initial linting failed due to fmt changes; fixed in second commit. - Added unit and integration tests (CI matrix includes kms-fake and sqlite job-runner).

Security review notes: - Priya and Lina performed threat modeling focusing on: replay attacks, signature spoofing, and key-residency leakage. Mitigations: include timestamp+nonce in envelope, rely on KMS key-hash and region tag, and no plaintext keys are persisted.

Open items: - We will iterate on the prooflet JSON-LD schema with Compliance (task ENG-4210). - Consider adding per-prooflet ACL if auditors request restricted access.

References: Linear ENG-4210 (prooflets design), internal RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4210/prooflets-rfc, and compliance ticket SUP-987.

Checklist:

- [x] Request plumbing and storage index
- [x] /internal/rbac/explain endpoint with sanitized output
- [x] DB migration and backfill job behind feature flag
- [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests
- [x] Console telemetry and docs stub

review_thread: Jared Wu: high level looks good. Can we make sure the prooflet index is sharded so it won't cause a single hot row on high-throughput tenants?
Maya Chen (author): added sharding hint in prooflet_backfill.go and added a shard_key in migration comments; made prooflet_index sharded by tenant hash.
Lina Ortega: Threat model OK but we need explicit TTL for prooflets in the retention policy to avoid unbounded storage growth.
Maya Chen (author): added retention config audit.prooflet.retention_days with default 365 and telemetry to track storage usage.
Priya Nair (security): Please ensure signature verification rejects unexpected region tags (we should not accept prooflets signed for eu-west in us-east tenant contexts).
Maya Chen (author): verification enforces region affinity; added unit test verifying mismatch is rejected and metric emitted.
